subject: forklift
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: forklift.mdl, in the place of the game's models/forklift.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/sat_globe.mdl, models/fungus.mdl, models/bm_leg.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, B, A, C where the asset was C, C, A, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The brief asks for a warehouse forklift with its driver in the seat. In every side view (LEFT, RIGHT, BACK, FRONT) the outline reads as a forklift: a tall mast with two uprights at the front, forks projecting forward, an overhead guard with a roof and rear posts, a white body over a red chassis, and a counterweight at the back. Nothing sticks out or is missing, and the top and below views agree.

M2.reason: Measured size is 186.6 long, 60 wide and 113.4 high against the brief's 187 long and 113 high (within 0.3%). The width of 60 is the brief's own figure, so the measure gives the same result as the brief.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies, checked down to the small ones: driver (yellow hard hat, green overalls, arms and legs visible in LEFT, RIGHT and BELOW), seat, overhead guard with roof and two rear posts, mast with two uprights, two forks, front drive wheels and rear wheels, counterweight body, carriage backrest with rails. All are present and in the right places in the side and angle views. The steering wheel is hard to pick out at this scale, so it is not charged.

M4.reason: The brief names no colours. The paint reads as a plausible warehouse forklift: white body and hood, red chassis with lettering, dark metal mast and forks, black tyres, dark roof mesh, green overalls and a yellow hard hat on the driver. Each region has a consistent material and colour across the views.

M5.reason: Surface detail is present and in place: red chassis lettering, the '2.2' decal on the body, the grille on the hood, the cylinders and rails on the mast, the wheel detail and the roof mesh. Nothing in the paint reads as a smear or a stray stripe.

M6.reason: Capped by the line-up test, as the rubric directs. Asked four times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve, the judges picked B, B, A, C, and the asset (C) was picked once in four. That is chance, so the asset passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The front is the mast with the forks, and the front is correct. The driver faces forward toward the forks, which the LEFT view shows through his arm reaching toward the steering wheel and the FRONT view shows through his face over the mast. The vehicle stands upright on its four wheels.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. The triangle count is 749, which is the most Valve spends on props of this size (the measured maximum) and so is not past the amended line. It is well above the third quartile (296), which the kit warns at but does not fail. Nothing visible is open, inside out or floating: the forks reach the ground, the wheels sit on it, and the carriage and body read as solid from the front and back. The underside cavities are not seen in play, which is Valve's practice.
